# The Why Sheet Press

> Print the argument. Carry it into the room. Free, CC0, editable advocacy sheets for families and educators
> navigating schools, hospitals and systems. Published by Stimpunks Foundation.

Every sheet is generated from Markdown in <https://github.com/Stimpunks/Why-Sheets>, which is the
source of truth.

**The Markdown source of any sheet is served directly.** Append .md to a sheet's URL —
<https://whysheet.press/sheets/hoodie.md> — and you get the file the page and the PDF are both
built from, with frontmatter carrying the canonical URL, the licence, when it last changed, and
links to its PDF and companion prompt. Each page also declares it with a
link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" element. There is no content negotiation on the
canonical URL: this site has no server. Each sheet page links its own source file. Everything is CC0 1.0 except quoted
material, which belongs to the people who wrote it.

## Why Sheets

- [Demand Avoidance](https://whysheet.press/sheets/demand-avoidance/): The refusal is a threat response, not defiance. Compliance pressure is the one reply guaranteed to escalate it — and the adjustments that do work are good teaching for every child. Reach for it when a school has decided a child is being defiant, and the child is drowning. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/demand-avoidance/
- [AAC Is Not a Last Resort](https://whysheet.press/sheets/aac/): A robust communication system is a right, not a reward for proving you deserve one — and AAC does not delay speech, it supports it. Reach for it when a school or clinic says a child needs to develop speech before they can have a communication system. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/aac/
- [Behaviorism](https://whysheet.press/sheets/behaviorism/): Behaviorism measures the surface, badly — and the primary legacy of ABA is trauma. Reach for it when compliance is being described as progress, and you need the evidence in one place. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/behaviorism/
- [Alternatives to ABA](https://whysheet.press/sheets/alternatives-to-aba/): Fourteen neurodiversity-affirming frameworks, gathered, so “what would you do instead” has an answer. Reach for it when you have said no to ABA and the room asks what you want instead. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/alternatives-to-aba/
- [ABA Tactics](https://whysheet.press/sheets/aba-tactics/): The tactics one by one — compliance training, extinction, quiet hands, forced eye contact — and what each one actually does. Reach for it when a programme is being described in technical language and you need to know what the words mean in a child’s day. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/aba-tactics/
- [Eye Contact](https://whysheet.press/sheets/eye-contact/): Forced eye contact is painful, it interferes with processing, and it is not evidence of attention. Reach for it in the meeting where eye contact is about to be written into a goal. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/eye-contact/
- [Masking and Burnout](https://whysheet.press/sheets/masking-and-burnout/): Masking is a stress response, not a skill. Burnout is the bill. Observation does not see either one. Reach for it when “but they’re fine at school” is being used to close a file. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/masking-and-burnout/
- [Monotropism](https://whysheet.press/sheets/monotropism/): Autistic experience explained through attention — and what stops looking like defiance once you can see the tunnel. Reach for it when transitions, “rigidity” or “obsession” are on the agenda. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/monotropism/
- [Developmental Pace](https://whysheet.press/sheets/developmental-pace/): Pace is ordinary variation, and it is uneven within one person. School treats it as fixed, sorts by birth date, and records the gap against the child. Reach for it when “working below age-related expectations” is being used as the reason to withhold something. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/developmental-pace/
- [Recess and Play](https://whysheet.press/sheets/recess-and-play/): Recess is regulation, not a privilege. Withholding it takes movement from the child who just showed you they need it — and who loses it is not random. Reach for it when recess is about to be withheld for behaviour or for unfinished work. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/recess-and-play/
- [Positive Greetings at the Door](https://whysheet.press/sheets/positive-greetings-at-the-door/): A greeting policy that turns a teacher into a threshold to be performed past. Reach for it when a school is adopting PGD and nobody has asked what it costs to walk through that door. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/positive-greetings-at-the-door/
- [Hoodie](https://whysheet.press/sheets/hoodie/): One page, already written, asking that a student wear a hoodie instead of the blazer. Reach for it when you need to hand the school a reason in writing, today. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/hoodie/
- [Sensory Access at Work](https://whysheet.press/sheets/sensory-access-at-work/): All eight senses, the common access needs at work, and the small changes that make a workplace livable. Reach for it in the accommodations conversation, when “what do you need?” needs a list rather than an apology. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/sensory-access-at-work/
- [Cavendish Space](https://whysheet.press/sheets/cavendish-space/): Caves, campfires and watering holes — vocabulary for a space that supports bodyminds instead of demanding they adapt. Reach for it when a room is being designed and you want words for what it should do. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/cavendish-space/
- [Neuroqueer Learning Spaces](https://whysheet.press/sheets/neuroqueer-learning-spaces/): The classroom as a bastion of neuronormativity, and what it takes to hold space against that. Reach for it when you are making the case for learning differently as a right, not a concession. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/neuroqueer-learning-spaces/
- [Queer and Neurodivergent Liberation are Entwined](https://whysheet.press/sheets/queer-and-neurodivergent-liberation-are-entwined/): Why the two movements share a history, a set of enemies, and a conversion-therapy lineage. Reach for it when someone asks why a neurodiversity organisation is talking about queerness. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/queer-and-neurodivergent-liberation-are-entwined/
- [Neuromodulation & Autism](https://whysheet.press/sheets/neuromodulation/): TMS, tDCS and what is being sold alongside them. The evidence base is weak and the framing is the pathology paradigm. Reach for it when a clinic or an advertisement offers a treatment and you have an appointment on Thursday. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/neuromodulation/
- [Boring Technology](https://whysheet.press/sheets/boring-technology/): Tools old, plain and open enough to outlive the companies that sell them. Reach for it when a service that holds someone’s access is about to be replaced by a platform. Also published at https://stimpunks.org/why/boring-technology/

## Companion prompts

Plain-text prompts a family pastes into their own AI assistant to draft an advocacy letter about
their own child. Each one interviews the reader first, then writes. Each embeds its sheet's
quotations verbatim with attribution and instructs the assistant to add no source it was not
given — because an invented or misattributed citation hands a school a reason to dismiss the
letter. Nothing is sent to us. CC0, like the sheets.

- [AAC Is Not a Last Resort](https://whysheet.press/prompts/aac.txt): a school letter from the AAC Is Not a Last Resort Why Sheet
- [ABA Tactics](https://whysheet.press/prompts/aba-tactics.txt): a school letter from the ABA Tactics Why Sheet
- [Alternatives to ABA](https://whysheet.press/prompts/alternatives-to-aba.txt): a school letter from the Alternatives to ABA Why Sheet
- [Behaviorism](https://whysheet.press/prompts/behaviorism.txt): a school letter from the Behaviorism Why Sheet
- [Demand Avoidance](https://whysheet.press/prompts/demand-avoidance.txt): a school letter from the Demand Avoidance Why Sheet
- [Developmental Pace](https://whysheet.press/prompts/developmental-pace.txt): a school letter from the Developmental Pace Why Sheet
- [Eye Contact](https://whysheet.press/prompts/eye-contact.txt): a school letter from the Eye Contact Why Sheet
- [Hoodie](https://whysheet.press/prompts/hoodie.txt): a school letter from the Hoodie Why Sheet
- [Masking and Burnout](https://whysheet.press/prompts/masking-and-burnout.txt): a school letter from the Masking and Burnout Why Sheet
- [Monotropism](https://whysheet.press/prompts/monotropism.txt): a school letter from the Monotropism Why Sheet
- [Neuromodulation & Autism](https://whysheet.press/prompts/neuromodulation.txt): a school letter from the Neuromodulation & Autism Why Sheet
- [Positive Greetings at the Door](https://whysheet.press/prompts/positive-greetings-at-the-door.txt): a school letter from the Positive Greetings at the Door Why Sheet

## Optional

- [About the press](https://whysheet.press/about/): where the form comes from, and the licence in plain words
- [Build a packet](https://whysheet.press/packet/): assemble several sheets into one paginated PDF
- [What changed](https://whysheet.press/changelog/): every release, newest first, in prose rather than commits
- [Feed](https://whysheet.press/feed.xml): RSS 2.0 of the same releases, for polling this site without scraping it
